Traces:
- trace(org, seed, preset, *, check=True, lesion=None, **world) -> Trace. One life in the pure-Python reference with read-only hooks. With check=True it raises unless F equals the kernel's F bitwise.
  - cells: uid, a, b, z, x, y, plane, cls, t_birth, t_death, death_cause, mother, mother_cid, k, row, n_spikes, n_rec.
  - knobs_birth / knobs_end: the 23 knobs, decoded with the kernel's decode.
  - genes_birth / genes_end: the 16 genes.
  - pheno_changes: changes of the gridded knobs at ticks.
  - spikes: t, cid, site, mask (the emit bits at fire time), kappa, cause, step, plus the dot and target position at the spike.
  - steps: membrane steps (v0, receptor input, refractory, fired).
  - arrivals: every arrival with its sender spike id and its contribution w_eff·mask.
  - receptors: delivered receptor events, with p_signal (the chance the event came from the target rather than background).
  - traj: dot and target at every integer time.
  - strokes: every act twitch with its exposed face and whether it pulled.
  - clicks (capture/miss), placements, ledger, meta.
- trace_kernel(org, seeds, preset, threads=2) -> list of KTrace (cells, knobs_birth, spikes, ledger). Fast and partial: no receptor events, no trajectory, and masks come from the emit bits at birth.
- relabel(tr, t_ref=None): role labels from the occupancy at T/2. Sense: C (centre), J (interior), S (rim). Act: K (hotspot), I (interior), M (rim). H for hidden.

Tuning:
- tuning(tr) -> one row per cell: rate vs target bearing from the dot (8 bins), vs distance from the dot, and vs distance from the cell's own point. Also vector strength vs, preferred bearing pref, and pref_minus_own. Act cells add n_pull, face, align (force-weighted cos of face vs target bearing) and toward.
- steering(tr): body-level align and toward, near and far.
- tuning_table(tun): compact text.

Flow:
- ccg(trs, max_lag=5, bin=0.25) -> neighbour-pair cross-correlograms pooled by (pre class, dir, post class). Columns include counts, expected, ratio, peak_lag, peak_ratio, sharp (peak over the median at lags of 2 or more), p_follow and lift. Works on Trace or KTrace lists.
- ccg_table(df): compact text.
- act_drivers(trs, window=(0.5, 3)) -> per act class, the share of act spikes preceded by: the own-column sense spike, sense spikes from other columns at ring 1 or within the radius, in-plane act neighbours, the hidden cell above, or nothing. Each share comes with its shuffled-time chance level. Also own_first and latency quartiles.
- drive_matrix(tr): for each class, which class fired it (the largest input of the firing step).
- chains(tr) -> each act spike traced back exactly through sender-spike links to its origin (rec, tonic, resid or unknown). Gives origin_dist, hops, lat_hops, latency, p_signal and the path, e.g. 'J[rec] S<lat M<down'.
- chain_summary(ch): rec_other_col, relayed, rec_signal, lat_by_hops, hops_share, top_paths.
- sense_drive(tr): what fired the sense cells, by class and ring.
- pathway_weights(tr): effective weights actually delivered, per (pre, travel, post) pathway.
- signature(trs): a dict of the router-vs-reflex numbers.
- pooled(fn, trs): runs a per-trace probe over several traces. report(tr): text report for one trace.

Lesions:
- lesion(org, preset, flags, t_fork, n_lives=128, seed0=SEED0, threads=2, t_open='fork', base_fork=0, **world) -> dict with base and lesion summaries, paired dF (lesioned minus base), captures, misses and n_end.

  - t_open='fork' counts F over [t_fork, T] only; pass 0 for the whole life.

- Lesion(t_fork, channels=3, slots='all'|'lateral'|'up'|'down'|'vertical', planes=None, sites=None, where=None): a per-cell, per-channel or per-direction message block in the reference. The sender still fires and pays.

- check_lesion_equivalence(org, preset, t_fork, seeds): asserts that a lateral Lesion equals the kernel's lateral_off bitwise.
- development_end(org, preset, n): quantiles of last birth time and end size.
- fmt_lesion(r): one-line text.

A rim sensor S (g_r 1, b 0.625) fires on any single receptor event and relays on ch0 to the motor directly above it (M.w0 1.5, kappa 1), which pulls outward. The centre sensor C drives the hotspot K. toolkit.router_signature:
router@ring4: 6 traced lives, mean F +9.50; every trace F equalled the kernel F bitwise.

Design: full rings 0-4. Interior sensors J (g_r 0.5, b 0.25, emit1 only) detect coincident receptor events and relay laterally on ch1. Rim sensors S listen to ch1 (w1 1.0), fire on one J relay as well as on their own receptor, and pass it up on ch0 to the rim motor M. So a target over the interior near one side makes that side's rim motors pull toward it. RESULTS.md: GS2 +2.25 over the best reflex; GS4 lateral_off removes 4.3 times that gain.

What separates a router from a reflex, most direct first:
1. chain_summary rec_other_col and relayed well above 0 (0.385 against exactly 0), with latency quantised at about d0 per hop.
2. sense_drive / drive_matrix: rim sensors fired by J(lat) arrivals (0.39 against 0).
3. Kernel-only proxy: a sharp lateral sense->sense CCG peak at lag about d0 (sharp 9-10 against about 1.5), together with lateral_off after development removing most of F (-9.3 against 0).

What does not separate them: whether the motor spike is preceded by its own column's sense spike. It is 1.00 in both, because in the router the own-column rim sensor is the last relay. The real question is what fired that sensor.

Smoke test on speck_lmax4_hexprism_sex_s5 (4 traced lives, F +6.1 to +8.8): the evolved body uses router-like lateral pooling in the sense plane.
- 32% of rim-motor spikes start in another column; 33% of rim-sensor spikes are fired laterally.
- Lateral sense weights are weak and excitatory: J->S +0.55, J->J +0.34.
- Sense cells act as coincidence detectors (b -0.65, g_r about 1.25; 57% of receptor events fire their cell; rec_signal 0.60).
- There is inhibitory feedback: act -> own sensor -1.3 to -1.6, hidden -> act -1.0 to -1.2.

interp.body: speck_lmax4_hexprism_sex_s5 (GRN body, genome sha1 032117bd..., preset catch_speck_l4). All life seeds are analysis.fresh_seeds(n, seed0=31_000_000). Six fully logged reference lives (seeds 31,000,000-31,000,005) each matched the kernel F bitwise, so the traces are the real lives.
interp.F_intact: Whole life: F +6.80 ± 0.08 over 1024 lives, with 20.0 captures and 20.1 misses per life. Income is 9.77 per unit time and cost 2.98 (living 2.32, secretion 0.29, misses 0.20, spikes/twitches/messages/receptor 0.11). Over [256, T] with division_off at 256, F is +7.39 (256 lives). On the same seeds the hand bodies score: reflex@hollow3 +8.58 ± 0.11 (20.8 captures, 45.1 misses, 56 cells); router@ring4 +10.80 ± 0.12 (28.1 captures, 45.4 misses, 122 cells). s5 captures about as often as the reflex and misses less than half as often. It scores lower because it carries twice the cells (living cost 2.32 against 1.12).
interp.anatomy: There are 122 cells at the end on average (q10 to q90: 104 to 140). Sense plane z=0 holds 56 (48 to 65), act plane z=1 holds 50 (43 to 58), hidden z>=2 holds 15 (10 to 21). The sense plane is a compact, irregular hexagonal disk out to ring 4 or 5; occupied sites per ring are 1, 6, 12, 17-18, 6-19, 0-10. The act plane covers the same disk minus 2 to 9 columns, mostly notches at the rim, with 0 to 3 enclosed holes. About 60% of act cells have an exposed face (rim motors M, about 34 per life). About 18 per life are interior (I) and cannot pull. The hidden cells form a small tower over the centre within ring 3: 6 to 13 cells at z=2 and 3 to 8 at z=3. Lineage: the zygote at (0,0,0) builds the sense plane by in-plane divisions (42 to 65 per life). Most act cells are daughters of the sense cell directly below them (33 to 50 vertical divisions); a few come from in-plane act divisions (4 to 8). Hidden cells come from central act cells (5 to 8) and stack once more. So each column is a sensor/motor pair of mother and daughter. Growth: median birth t about 20, 90% of births by t 45 to 112, and about 95% of the final cells exist by t=256. Rare late births continue until t about 840 to 980, but division_off at 256 changes nothing (dF +0.03 ± 0.17). No cell dies (p_die is 0).

cell_types.name: rim sensor S (high-gain coincidence detector)
cell_types.where: outer ring of the sense disk
cell_types.knobs: w0 +1.12, w1 -0.81 (k-means rim cluster: -0.76), b -0.69, g_r +1.35 (rim cluster 1.41), tau_m 4, t_ref 0.5, emit0=emit1=1, kappa 1 (twitch has no effect at z=0), delta 0, a0 +0.63, a1 -0.99, tau_tr 2, phi 0
cell_types.role: Fires on 2 receptor events within about 5.5 units, or 1 event plus 1-2 recent neighbour spikes. Its spike drives the motor above it with +2.5. Its gain is about 0.15 higher than interior sensors' (a different gene state from fewer neighbours, via n_view), so it has a longer coincidence window.

cell_types.name: interior sensor J and centre sensor C (coincidence detector)
cell_types.where: interior of the sense disk; C at (0,0,0)
cell_types.role: Same rule as S, with a coincidence window of about 4.6 units. J drives an interior act cell I (wasted pull) or, under act-plane gaps, a rim motor. J gives lateral support to its neighbours (+0.33 to J, +0.6 to rim S). C drives the hotspot K.

cell_types.name: rim motor M
cell_types.where: act cells with at least one empty in-plane neighbour site (outer rim, notches, holes)
cell_types.role: Follows its own sensor 1:1 (input +2.5, one spike fires it, latency 1.0). Each twitch pulls the dot along its open-face normal, outward, toward a target lying over that column. Its spike sends -1.1 to -1.6 back down to its sensor, plus +1.7 up to any hidden cell.

cell_types.name: interior act cell I and hotspot K
cell_types.where: act cells with all 6 neighbours present; K at (0,0,1)
cell_types.role: I is the same follower as M but cannot pull (only 1-3% of its twitches move the dot). Its role is to return delayed inhibition (-1.6) to the interior sensor below it. K is fired by C (98%); each K twitch at least 3.5 units after the previous one clicks (no twitch within 2 units of the previous one ever clicks).

cell_types.name: hidden H (two subtypes)
cell_types.where: small tower over the centre, ring <= 3
cell_types.role: Follows the act cell below (+1.7 to +2.1) and inhibits it (-1.0 to -1.2). Functionally inert: hidden_off dF +0.04 ± 0.16; F is reproduced without hidden lateral messages.

interp.channels:
Every cell emits every spike on both channels, in every cell for the whole life (emit0 = emit1 = 1). Channel 0 is nominally excitatory (w0 +1.0 to +1.12 in all cells) and channel 1 nominally inhibitory (w1 -0.56 to -0.88). Each receiver re-weights the two channels per input slot with its morphogen polarity: w_eff = q8(w·(1 + a·shat)), with a0 +0.6 to +1.4, a1 -1.0 to -2.0, shat ≈ +1 on the slot below and ≈ -1 on the slot above. This gives three distinct pathway signs from one genome-wide pair:
- From below (sense to act, act to hidden): ch0 +2.0 (clipped) and ch1 flipped positive at +0.5 to +0.9, total +2.5 to +2.8. One spike fires the receiver.
- From above (act to sensor, hidden to act): ch0 +0.26 to +0.6 and ch1 -1.6 to -1.9, total -1.1 to -1.6. Inhibitory.
- In-plane: ch0 +0.9 to +1.26 and ch1 -0.67 to -0.97, net about +0.3 (J to rim S +0.6). The weak excitation is a near-cancellation of E and I.

Who sends what:
- Sensors excite the act cell above and weakly excite their sense neighbours.
- Act cells inhibit the sensor below, excite the hidden cell above, and send weak, mixed-sign lateral messages (M to M +0.12, I to M +0.28, M to I -0.16).
- Hidden cells inhibit the act cell below.
- No cell changes its emit bits. pheno_fixed after 256 has no effect (dF -0.04 ± 0.18), so the circuit is fixed after development even though gridded knobs change about 60 to 86 times per cell after 256.
interp.algorithm_plain:
Each column is a reflex arc. Its sensor sits about 0.65 below threshold (b ≈ -0.67), so one receptor event (+1.25 to +1.4) almost never fires it on its own: 11% of isolated events. It fires on a coincidence: a second own event within about 4.6 units (interior) or 5.5 units (rim), or one event plus 1 to 3 recent spikes from neighbouring sensors (+0.3 each, +0.6 from J to a rim S). For a fresh event, P(fire) is 0.11, 0.42, 0.69, 0.86, 0.94 with 0, 1, 2, 3, 4+ neighbour spikes in the previous 3 units, and 0.96 with one earlier own event.

Because the target's halo (sigma 0.6) puts events into a cluster of about 7 neighbouring sensors at once, this spatial and temporal coincidence rule passes target events (84% fire) and rejects most background events (29% fire). Half of all sensor spikes needed lateral help: they would not have crossed threshold without it.

A sensor spike fires the act cell above it about 1.0 later (+2.5, 99%). That twitch pulls the dot along the column's open face, outward, so a target over the rim on one side drags the dot toward itself. Pulls are aimed better than either hand body's (align +0.30, 73% toward).

About 1.0 after the twitch, the act cell sends -1.1 to -1.6 back to its own sensor. A sensor that just fired is reset to 0, above its rest of -0.65, so it is primed: a single event fires it again (P 0.75 within 1 unit). The returning inhibition cancels that priming (P falls to 0.32 to 0.41, the baseline). This keeps the weakly excitatory sense sheet from spreading activity sideways. Without the feedback, sensors fire on almost every event, off-target sensor spikes triple, lateral arrivals become their main driver, and pull aim collapses from 0.45 to 0.10.

As the dot closes in, the target passes over the interior, where act cells have no open face, so the pulling stops by itself. When the centre sensor C fires (target within about 1 of the dot), K twitches, and if K's twitch has decayed since the last press, the hotspot clicks. Click precision is about 55%; 4.8 of 5 misses are near misses at distance 1.1 to 2.

Hidden cells and the K-to-C feedback play no measurable role. Act-plane lateral coupling is a backup: it matters only when sense-plane lateral coupling is gone.
interp.pseudocode:
every cell: event-driven LIF, theta 1, tau 4, t_ref 0.5, reset to v=0 (rest b<0, so a cell that just fired is primed);
  each spike goes on ch0 and ch1 to all live neighbours, delay ~1;
  receiver's morphogen polarity sets the per-slot weight: from below +2.5, from above -1.1..-1.6, in-plane +0.3 (J->rim S +0.6)

SENSOR s (z=0), rest -0.67:
  on receptor event:            v += g_r          # 1.25 interior, 1.4 rim; alone -> v ~ 0.6 < 1
  on neighbour sensor spike:    v += 0.3..0.6
  on spike of act cell above:   v -= 1.1..1.6     # arrives ~2 after s fired: cancels the post-spike priming
  if v >= 1: spike  -> act cell above (+2.5), sense neighbours (+0.3)
  # effective rule: fire iff (2 own events within ~4.6-5.5) or (1 event + 1-3 neighbour spikes within ~3)
  #                 or (1 event within ~2 of its own last spike, before the feedback lands)

ACT cell m above s (z=1), rest -0.5..-0.6:
  on spike from s: v += 2.5 -> spike (99%), latency 1.0
  on spike: twitch kappa=1
       if m has an empty in-plane neighbour: dot += pull along the open-face normal (outward)
       if m is the hotspot (0,0,1) and its twitch has decayed below 0.25: CLICK (capture if target within 1)
       send -1.1..-1.6 down to s; +1.7 up to the hidden cell; +-0.1..0.3 to act neighbours (backup only)
HIDDEN: follow the act cell below, inhibit it; no effect on F.

emergent loop: target halo over rim columns -> cooperative detection -> rim motors pull toward it
  -> target drifts over the interior (no open faces, pulling stops) -> C fires -> K clicks

interp.vs_handbuilt:
In its wiring it is reflex-like: 89% of motor spikes are fired by the sensor directly below, one hop, latency 1.0. This is the same 1:1 column arc as reflex@hollow3, with reflex-like receptive fields and reach. It is not a router. Router signatures are only half present: rec_other_col 0.30 (router 0.385, reflex 0); J->S CCG sharp 3.4 (router 9.4, reflex 1.5); lateral_off loses 63% (router 87%, reflex 0%). More importantly, the lateral messages mostly facilitate cells that have their own evidence (30-40% cooperative spikes, against 2% in the router's rim cells) rather than relay other columns' detections (9-21% against 36%), and they do not widen rim receptive fields.

The new part is that each sensor is a coincidence detector in a weakly excitatory, E/I-balanced sheet. The sheet is kept sparse by delayed inhibition from the motor layer above, so the act cells double as the sense layer's inhibitory interneurons. All synapse signs come from one E/I channel pair re-weighted by morphogen polarity: up excites, down inhibits, sideways nearly balances. This is closest to an excitable medium with layer-supplied refractoriness, a cooperative and noise-filtering detector.

It is not a pacemaker or oscillator (no tonic cells; b < 0 everywhere), not winner-take-all, and not hotspot-gated (the into-centre and K->C lesions are null). Its lower F than the reflex comes from cost, not skill: about twice the cells, with similar captures and fewer than half the misses.
interp.interesting:
1. One genome-wide channel pair (w0 ≈ +1.1, w1 ≈ -0.85) plus a morphogen-polarity anisotropy gives three pathway signs. Feedforward (up) is +2.5; channel 1 flips sign here. Feedback (down) is -1.1 to -1.6. Lateral is a near-cancellation at +0.3. The inhibitory channel's anisotropy (a1 ≈ -1 to -2) is what makes the feedforward arc suprathreshold.
2. The act layer doubles as the sense layer's inhibitory interneurons. Interior act cells, which can never pull, still deliver -1.6 to their sensors. Removing all downward feedback costs more F (-5.6) than removing all lateral messages (-4.7), because the sense sheet then runs away: off-target spikes triple and aim collapses.
3. Reset-to-0 above a negative rest makes every spike prime the sensor, so it would burst. The motor's inhibition arrives about 2 units after the sensor spike, in time to cancel exactly that priming.
4. The lateral pathways in two planes are redundant: act-plane coupling matters only when sense-plane coupling is removed (interaction -1.77 ± 0.60).
5. Correlation and causation diverge at the hotspot. 78% of captures follow centre spikes that needed lateral support, yet blocking that support changes F by -0.20 ± 0.39: centre spikes from its own receptor events alone take over.
6. Lateral pooling is tuned to the trained target. With sigma 1.0 instead of 0.6, removing it raises F by 60%; the hand router shows the same reversal (+5.7).
7. The evolved body aims better than both hand bodies (align +0.30 against +0.18 and +0.23) and misses half as often. It loses on F only through living cost, and through about 40% of act cells sitting in the interior where their twitches cannot pull.

verify.corrected_algorithm:
What survives:

Development settles a fixed sheet of two-cell columns by about t=256. Each column is a sensor in the sense plane with a motor directly above it.

Sensors are timing-based coincidence detectors. Bias is about -0.66, receptor gain about 1.25 in the interior and 1.36 at the rim, membrane time constant 4. One receptor event never fires a resting sensor. Two of its own events do, if they arrive within about 4.6 units (interior) or 5-6 units (rim). This two-event rule alone is what makes target events fire sensors about 2.5 times as often as background events.

A sensor spike fires the act cell above it about 1 unit later (weight +2.5, 99% of the time). A rim act cell's twitch pulls the dot outward through its open face. The centre sensor fires the hotspot cell (99%), which clicks when its last twitch has decayed.

Lateral messages are weak excitation (+0.3; interior-to-rim +0.6), the near-cancellation of an excitatory and an inhibitory channel. They spread sub-threshold excitation from sensors under the target to their neighbours, including sensors 1.5-3 units outside the target's halo that receive no target events. Those primed sensors then fire on a sparse background event, or on 3-4 neighbour spikes arriving together. A parallel act-plane lateral path (interior-to-rim motor +0.28) partly backs this up.

The effect is not a uniform gain:
- No uniform bias or receptor-gain substitute recovers F.
- Rim receptive fields are 4-5 times wider beyond 1.5 units.
- Most importantly, when the target sits over the body's interior (1-3 units from the dot), the recruited rim motors on the target's side keep pulling toward it (aim +0.45 to +0.6).

So lateral spread drives the final approach and the captures (approach speed at 1-3 units doubles), not long-range pursuit beyond 3-4 units. It is a soft, router-like recruitment: lateral excitation primes the sensors, and each sensor's own background events or summed lateral inputs trigger it, rather than one-hop relays. The benefit is tuned to the trained target size: it disappears at sigma ≈ 0.84 and turns into a cost at sigma 0.9-1.0.

Every act cell, including interior ones that can never pull, sends inhibition of -1.2 to -1.6 back down to its own sensor, arriving about 2 units after the sensor spiked. This feedback is what stops the laterally coupled sheet from over-recruiting and reverberating; without it, aim collapses and off-target spikes triple. It matters only when lateral coupling is present: with lateral messages off, removing it costs nothing. Its trimming of the sensor's post-spike priming is minor.

Hidden cells are inert. The a1 polarity term is not singularly responsible for the feedforward arc.
verify.simplest_alternative:
The simplest alternative is a plain column reflex, where each sensor drives the act cell above it, plus incidental lateral excitation. Its variants are:
- lateral messages acting only as a uniform excitability/gain boost;
- lateral messages mattering only through cost or development.

All of these are ruled out:
- Lateral_off after development costs -4.3 to -4.9 F, all of it reward; every cost term changes by 0.05 or less. This holds with the fork at 256 or 512, with division_off or freeze in both arms, and over the whole life with growth unchanged.
- Seven uniform sensor-gain substitutes under lateral_off never recover F (best -4.2).
- A gain-matched substitute with the intact spike and pull counts still loses -4.6. It halves aim and destroys background rejection.

Note that the claim's own summary of the lateral role ("detection gain, not direction") is essentially this ruled-out alternative. The surviving lateral role is spatial recruitment of off-halo rim motors during the final approach.

interp.channels:
Channel 0 is sent only by sense cells (every sense cell has emit0=1, emit1=0). It is received by:
- in-plane sense neighbours, with w0 ≈ +1.05. Delivered after t=512 this is +0.97 to +1.03 between covered cells and C0, never negative; +1.54 inward from the fringe; and -0.14 to -0.25, 57-60% negative, when moving outward into fringe cells. These are excitatory and carry the whole lateral effect.
- the act cell above, with w0 = +2.0 (+1.99 delivered). One arrival fires it.
Hidden cells never receive ch0.

Channel 1 is sent only by act cells and 74% of hidden cells. It is received by:
- in-plane act neighbours, with w1 +0.27 to +0.5 (+0.16 to +0.5 delivered). This is weak and subthreshold: the act-plane lateral lesion gives +0.19 ± 0.44.
- the sense cell below, with w1 ≈ -0.5 (inhibitory). It arrives about 2 units after that sense cell fired, inside its 3.3 refractory period, so almost all of it is lost (about 100 non-refractory arrivals in 12 lives). It has no function.
- hidden cells above, -0.5 to -1.9 delivered, which keeps them silent.

In short: excitation flows sense→sense and sense→act on ch0. ch1 is effectively unused. The only effective "inhibition" is the outward-negative weight into fringe cells.
interp.algorithm_plain:
1. **Development.** The body grows a two-layer topographic sheet. A wide sense disk (radius about 5) carries a smaller motor disk (radius about 4) made of cells budded straight up from sense cells. About a third of the sensors form a motor-less fringe. Hidden cells are silent.
2. **Sensing.** Each sensor is a leaky coincidence counter. Its rest is -1.7 and its threshold 1 (time constant 2). An own receptor event adds +2 and a neighbour sensor's spike adds about +1, so a rested sensor needs about 2 "votes" within about 2 time units, at least one of them usually its own:
   - P(fire) for 1 own event alone is 0.05; for 1 neighbour spike alone, 0.001;
   - own event plus 1-2 neighbour spikes: 0.86-1.0; two own events: 0.995; 3-4 neighbour spikes alone: 0.41-0.85.
   A target halo (sigma 0.6) that covers a patch of sensors therefore turns sparse Poisson events into a burst of mutually confirming spikes. Isolated background events (0.05 per unit) rarely fire anything.
3. **Latch.** After a spike the sensor is refractory for about 3.3 units, then restarts at v=0 instead of -1.7. For about 1.8 units a single own event (or about 2 neighbour spikes) fires it again. Starting a detection is hard; keeping it going is easy. While the target stays within about 1 unit, the sensor fires about once every 3.5-4 units.
4. **Lateral excitation widens the detection map.** Each sensor's receptive field grows from about 1.2 to about 2+ units, while the peak rate stays the same because the refractory period caps it. Fringe sensors relay detections inward (+1.5), so targets beyond the motor footprint also activate covered sensors. Outward messages into the fringe are weak or negative. Lateral activity never spreads on its own: it needs receptor evidence at each step, and only 7% of motor chains have 3 or more hops.
5. **Steering.** Every covered-sensor spike fires the motor directly above about 1 unit later (99.9% of motor spikes). A rim motor's twitch pulls the dot outward along its open face, so the body drifts toward whichever side of its rim lies over the active patch. The widened map roughly doubles the number of pulls and the useful thrust when the target is 1-6 units away, at equal per-pull alignment.
6. **Clicking.** The centre sensor works the same way. Each of its spikes drives the hotspot motor, and each of those is a click. A capture happens when the target is within 1 unit at that moment (85 of 85 such clicks were captures; every click with the target beyond 1 was a miss). Lateral input into the centre sensor makes it click liberally when the target is near but not yet under it. That buys a few captures at the price of many cheap misses (10 per miss against 500 per capture).
7. **Nothing else.** There is no spontaneous activity (receptor_off leaves 2 spikes in 512 units), no oscillator, no functional inhibition, no hidden computation, and nothing that depends on ongoing gene-driven knob changes after development (freeze +0.27 ± 0.18).

```
# every sense cell i (z=0); end-of-life knobs, near-identical in all sense cells
REST=-1.7; TAU=2; THR=1; TREF=3.3; G_R=+2.0
on own receptor event:        v_i += 2.0
on ch0 spike from sense nbr j: v_i += w_ji   # ~+1.0 covered<->covered, +1.5 fringe->inward, <=0 inward->fringe
on ch1 from act cell above:   v_i += -0.5    # lands during refractory: no effect
between events: v_i = REST + (v_i - REST) * exp(-dt/TAU)
if v_i >= THR and not refractory(i):
    send ch0 to 6 sense nbrs and to act cell above (delay ~1)
    refractory for TREF, then restart at v_i = 0       # not at REST -> ~1.8u 'primed' window
# effective rule
#   rested: fire iff within ~2u  [2 own events] or [1 own event + >=1 nbr spike] or [>=3-4 nbr spikes]
#   primed: fire on [1 own event] or [~2 nbr spikes]

# act cell k directly above sense cell i (z=1): b=-0.7, w0=+2  -> fires ~1u after every spike of i
on spike of k: twitch(kappa=1)
    if k has open faces: pull dot along sum of open-face unit vectors (outward)
    if k is hotspot (0,0,1): click   # capture iff |target - dot| <= 1
# hidden cells: inhibited by act spikes, never fire
```

interp.vs_handbuilt:
It is a hybrid, closest to the router by the toolkit's criteria but different in mechanism. I would call it neighbour-assisted coincidence detection.

**Router-like:**
- 31% of motor spikes originate (by largest input) in another column: router 38.5%, reflex 0, s5 32%.
- 28% of sense spikes are fired by a lateral arrival (router 27%).
- Chain latency is quantised at about d0 per hop.
- Lateral_off after development removes 54-57% of F (reflex 0%).
- The motor-less fringe relays inward like the router's interior J cells.

**Not a router:**
- The router's relay is an OR: one J relay fires a rim S. Here a single lateral spike essentially never fires a rested sensor (P 0.001); it must coincide with own receptor evidence (0.86-1.0). That is why the lateral CCG is only sharp 2.3-3.7, against 9.4 for the router.
- Pooling among covered sensors is isotropic. It is a spatial vote that widens and densifies a topographic detection map, not a routing of interior evidence to a particular rim.

**Motor side is pure reflex:** each act cell is a 1-hop follower of the sense cell directly below (99.9%), and pulls along its own face.

**Ruled out:** no inhibition-based contrast (the ch1 feedback lands in refractoriness), no pacemaker or oscillator (receptor_off leaves 2 spikes in 512 units), no self-propagating wave (each hop needs receptor support; ≥3-hop chains are 7%), no winner-take-all, no hidden layer. The hotspot is just another sensor plus follower; its lateral pooling produces liberal clicking rather than gating.

**New relative to both hand-built bodies:**
- the post-spike latch (hard to start, easy to continue);
- the morphogen-built inward funnel at the fringe.

The same lateral-pooling signature was seen in the s5 smoke test, so this may be a recurring evolved solution.
interp.interesting:
1. **Hysteresis from the reset rule.** A fired cell restarts at v=0 while its rest is -1.7, so for about 1.8 units after its refractory period a single receptor event re-fires it, where a rested cell needs about 2 votes. Evolution turned an ABI detail into a latch: detection is hard to start and easy to sustain. Removing it costs -0.90 ± 0.30 F.
2. **Anatomy as a by-product of development.** Act cells only bud straight up (96%), so the sense disk outgrows the motor disk. The motor-less fringe became an antenna. Morphogen anisotropy (a0 = -2) makes its connections directional: inward excitation +1.5, outward weak or negative. That gives about 38% of the lateral benefit.
3. **Maturation schedule.** Sense b drifts from about -0.9 at birth to -1.7 by age 512, and t_ref from 1.9 to 3.4. Young sensors are single-event, reflex-like detectors; mature ones become cooperative coincidence detectors (correlational, life 0).
4. **Activity-dependent b exists but is not used.** b steps up after more receptor events (2.4 vs 0.66 events in the prior 8 units for up vs down changes), yet freezing everything at 512 costs nothing (+0.27 ± 0.18).
5. **Tuned amplifier.** The lateral network is tuned to the trained background. At 4 times the background it runs away (82 misses per half-life) and turning it off helps (+2.07).
6. **Hotspot pooling exploits the prices.** A miss costs 10 and a capture pays 500, so lateral drive into the centre sensor makes about 8 extra misses per half-life to buy about 0.8 captures.
7. **Clean click mechanics.** 98% of hotspot spikes are clicks, because the centre sensor's t_ref (3.4-3.5) plus the hotspot's own refractoriness keeps spikes beyond the key re-arm time (3.47).
8. **Waste.** About 11 interior motors twitch without a face, and the hidden cells are silent dead weight.

verify.corrected_algorithm:
1. **Body.** The body grows a two-layer topographic sheet. A sense disk (about 57 cells, radius about 5) carries a smaller motor disk (about 37 cells) whose cells were budded straight up from the sensors. Sensors with no motor above form a fringe of about 20 cells. The 0-13 hidden cells never fire. After t of about 512 the network is effectively fixed: freezing all knobs costs nothing.

2. **Sensors.** Each sensor is a leaky integrator: rest about -1.7, threshold 1, time constant 2.
   - An own receptor event adds +2.
   - A neighbour sensor's spike (channel 0) adds about +1.1 between sensors under the motors.
   - Fringe sensors send about +1.6 to +1.9 inward. Messages moving outward into the fringe carry about 0 or a negative weight.
   - So a rested sensor fires on a weighted 2-vote rule within about 2 units, with its own event counting double:
     - two own events: about 1.0;
     - one own event plus one neighbour spike: 0.82-0.87;
     - three or four neighbour spikes: 0.38-0.82;
     - one own event alone: 0.04;
     - one neighbour spike alone: 0.002.
   - After a spike the sensor is refractory for about 3.3, then restarts at 0. For about 1.8 units a single event re-fires it (the ABI reset rule); removing this costs about 1.4 F.

3. **Motors.** Every sensor spike fires the motor directly above it about 1 unit later (99%). A rim motor pulls the dot outward along its open face. The hotspot motor above the centre sensor clicks.

4. **What the lateral messages do.** Sensor-to-sensor lateral excitation carries about 55% of F after development, entirely as capture reward. It works because it is spatially specific: neighbours that share the same target confirm each other's sparse receptor events, and fringe cells funnel evidence inward. Covered-sensor output is worth about 1.8 F and fringe output about 1.3 F.
   - Delivering the same lateral drive to random sensors is worse than having none.
   - A uniform excitability increase on a lateral-free body, up to a pure single-event reflex, recovers at most about 20% of the loss.

5. **Clicking.** Lateral input into the centre sensor mostly adds cheap miss clicks (86% of the miss change) and only a few captures (about 14%).

6. **Stability and tuning.** The pooling is an amplifier kept stable partly because about a third of the lateral echoes land in refractory neighbours. If they are misplaced or delayed, activity runs away. It is tuned to the trained background: it helps at lam_bg up to 0.10 and hurts by 0.15. As the signal strengthens it stops improving capture efficiency and only helps steering. Act-plane lateral messages, the act-to-sensor feedback and the hidden cells do nothing measurable.
verify.simplest_alternative:
The simplest alternative is a plain column reflex (each sensor drives the motor above it) whose lateral excitation is only non-specific gain, or whose lateral messages matter only through cost or development timing. All of these were ruled out on fresh lives:
- **Cost:** every lesion saves cost; the whole loss is reward.
- **Development timing:** the effect is unchanged with both arms frozen, with division_off, and with the fork at 768.
- **Uniform gain:** blocking lateral messages and shifting all sensor biases (db 0.1-0.75, including the spike-count-matched 0.4 and a pure single-event reflex at 0.75) recovers at most +0.64 +- 0.26 of the 3.3 loss.
- **Placement:** scrambling where the lateral drive lands, while keeping its amount and timing, gives -4.15 +- 0.39, worse than no lateral messages at all.
The spatial pooling is real and necessary.

interp.anatomy:
A filled two-layer hexagonal disc that never stops growing. It adds about 0.05 cells per unit time. Mean cells alive: 30 at t=128, 46 at 256, 72 at 512, 90 at 768 and 108 at 1024 (48 lives). Only 43% of the final cells exist by t=256, the last birth is at about t=1010, and no cell ever dies.

End of life (256 lives):
- Sense plane: 54.9 cells. Rings 0-3 are almost full, ring 4 is about half full and ring 5 has a few cells.
- Act plane: 48.8 cells. Every act cell sits directly on a sense cell, and there are no act-only columns. There are 2-11 sense-only columns. One of them is always an enclosed hole in the act plane at ring 2, seen in all 6 traced lives.
- Hidden cells (z=2, rarely z=3): 4.65 per life (range 2-10). They are born early (t ≈ 25-200) from act-cell mothers over rings 0-3.

Lineage: sense cells build both planes. Each sense cell divides sideways (a new sense cell) and upward (the act cell above it); 96-99% of act cells have a sense-cell mother. Act cells divide almost only to bud hidden cells.

The GRN uses 8 active genes and reads n_view (W weights up to ±9.8), its own activity traces f, r0 and rho, and the plane cues. It retunes the knobs every ~2 units: about 13,000 gridded knob changes per life.

interp.channels:
Only channel 0 is used. Every cell has emit0=1 and emit1=0, except a few hidden cells: in 6 lives, 11 of 170,857 arrivals carried channel 1. So w1 has no effect.

Each message's sign and size are set by the receiver's anisotropy. All cells have a0 = −2 and pol1 ≈ 1.75, and pol1 reads a morphogen-1 gradient that is higher in the act plane. That gives w_eff = w0·(1 − 2·ŝ):
- **Up, sense → act (ŝ = −1, ×3), strong excitation:** S→M +0.93 (median 1.0-1.125), J→M +0.77, J→I +0.69, C→K +0.68 (median 0.75).
- **Down, act → sense (ŝ = +1, ×−1), weak inhibition:** M→S −0.10, I→J −0.10, K→C −0.13. It is never decisive, because a receptor event adds +2. Making sense cells deaf to the cell above: dF −0.07 ± 0.34, misses +1.7 ± 0.5.
- **Lateral, act plane, excitatory and biased outward:** outward 0.33, sideways 0.26, inward 0.155. By pair: I→M 0.33, M→M 0.24, I→I 0.21, I→K 0.23, M→K 0.15.
- **Lateral, sense plane, weak:** J→J 0.10, S→S 0.11, S→J 0.16, J→S 0.06.

So:
- Sense cells send to the act cell above (excite) and to sense neighbours (negligible).
- Act cells send to act neighbours (excite, outward) and to the sensor below (mildly inhibit).
- Hidden cells listen to act cells but are nearly silent.
interp.algorithm_plain:
s2 runs a column reflex in a growing two-layer disc. It adds two GRN-made controls: a gain map that switches act cells on according to whether they can pull, and a leaky click gate that the GRN keeps tight while the neighbourhood is busy. There is no tonic or pacemaker activity: with receptor_off the whole body falls silent (0 spikes).

1. **Sensing.** Each screen point under the body has a sense cell that fires once for every receptor event it receives (g_r 2). The sense plane does no computation; it is a 1-bit retina.

2. **Relay up.** A sense spike goes upward with ×3 weight, made from one small weight plus a vertical polarity. The act cell above decides by its gain:
   - Act cells with an exposed face (the rim, and the edges of holes) have gain 1.125. They relay every sensor spike and pull the dot outward along that face, so the target sitting over a rim column pulls the dot toward itself.
   - Enclosed act cells, which cannot pull, have gain 0.75. They fire only when two inputs coincide within about 2 units, so isolated background events mostly die there. They pass activity outward to the rim through outward-biased lateral excitation (0.33 outward against 0.16 inward). A target over the interior near one side therefore recruits the rim motors on that side.
   - This act-plane relay costs captures in small bodies and gains them in large ones. The crossover is at about 70-75 cells, and the body grows to about 108 cells.

3. **Clicking.** The hotspot K is an enclosed cell, so C→K is only 0.75. K behaves as a leaky integrator of C spikes plus lateral act chatter, and fires when about 2 inputs arrive within about 2 units. When the target is centred, C fires at about 1 per unit time and K fires and clicks. The key re-arms only after about 3.5 units of K silence, which limits clicks within a burst. Isolated background events at C still pass the gate 44% of the time, and 78% of misses start from background events.
   - K's GRN reads its arrivals trace r0. Neighbourhood activity keeps K in the tight state (tau 2, b 0.125). Silence lets it drift to a loose state (tau 4, b 0.25) that clicks on more background. Very strong activity pushes it tighter still (w0 0.125, b 0).
   - Freezing K, or blinding it to r0, leaves it stuck in the loose state part of the time, and misses rise 40-60%.
   - Clamping K at its usual tight state performs like the intact body. Clamping it looser or tighter, or giving it a one-spike trigger, is worse.

**Established causally:**
- Everything is receptor-driven, and the vertical relay is required (receptor_off and motor_off).
- The sense plane's own dynamics and lateral messages do not matter: freeze sense-plane GRNs, freeze C, an act-only lateral block that reproduces kernel lateral_off.
- The hotspot gate's operating point (K clamps, K_gain, K_lat0).
- K's activity-held state (freeze K, blind K to r0 but not f).
- Interior damping prevents false clicks (int_gain_up raises misses).
- Lateral act messages have a sign that depends on body size (5 fork times; an across-life size split; the act-only block at 90 cells).
- Hidden cells are dispensable.

**Mostly correlational:**
- That the gain map is computed from neighbour count (structure, k-means clusters, all 6 observed enclosures followed by a gain drop).
- That rim relays carry the steering. The causal test, capping rim gain, was only −0.82 ± 0.49.
- That outward bias is why relays help large bodies (direction-split weights; approach speed in 4 traces).

interp.vs_handbuilt:
At its core it is reflex-like, plus an act-plane relay that only pays in large bodies, plus a hotspot gate.

**Reflex-like:**
- The sense plane fires only on its receptors (98% against 100% in the reflex and 61-73% in the router). Lateral sense CCG sharp is 1.4-1.8 (reflex 1.5, router 9.4).
- The S→M up relay has sharp 9.7 at lag of about 1.
- Receptive fields match the reflex's S.
- Steering is 0.13/0.59 against the reflex's 0.18/0.64.

**Unlike the reflex:**
- 33% of rim-motor chains start in another column (router 0.385, reflex 0). Those relays run through the act plane (I→M, M→M, outward-biased), not through the sense plane as in the router and s5.
- lateral_off is neither 0 (reflex) nor −9.3 (router). It changes sign with body size: +0.6 at 46 cells, −1.4 at 90.

**New compared with both:**
- A GRN-made gain map that switches on only the act cells that can pull.
- A hotspot that is a leaky two-input gate whose tight state is held by neighbourhood activity through the GRN, rather than a one-spike relay (C→K +1.5 in the hand bodies).

**Performance:** captures are 0.62 of the reflex's (12.2 against 20.5 on the same seeds) and misses 0.65 of the reflex's. With a 108-cell body, living cost is 1.33. F is +4.16 against +8.42 (reflex) and +10.99 (router).
interp.interesting:
1. **Directed wiring from one knob.** a0 = −2, reading a morphogen gradient, turns a single isotropic weight into ×3 excitation upward, ×−1 inhibition downward and an outward-biased lateral relay. Direction comes from a field, not from the anatomy.
2. **Cells set their gain by whether they can pull.** Act-cell gain tracks the exposed face, which cells cannot see directly: their GRN infers it from neighbour count. 0 of 103 enclosed cells have high gain, and cells that become enclosed drop their gain about 7 units later.
3. **Whether s2 counts as a router depends on its size.** In-plane messages hurt a 46-cell body (+0.59 when removed) and help a 90-cell body (−1.42). Growth keeps moving it across the crossover at about 70-75 cells.
4. **Activity-dependent settings (intrinsic plasticity) at the hotspot.** The hotspot's in-life GRN state is functional. Freezing it costs −1.1 F, and blinding it to its arrivals trace raises misses by 54%. But a fixed tight clamp is just as good, so the GRN is holding K away from a bad loose default rather than computing anything adaptive.
5. **The cost structure, not precision, sets the click rule.** A capture is worth 50 misses, so even a one-spike trigger that doubles misses costs F only within noise. Over-damping is the expensive error: captures −46%. The key's re-arm rule wastes 44% of K spikes in bursts.
6. **Every life has an enclosed act-plane hole at ring 2.** The cells around it get high gain and can pull inward.

speck_lmax4_hexprism_sex_s2 (catch_speck_l4). All new lives use analysis.fresh_seeds(n, seed0=31_250_000).

What was run:
- Kernel: 512 lives per arm for every fork, cap and lam_bg contrast.
- Reference, logged: 10 intact twins with growth frozen at 512. All 10 had F bitwise equal to the kernel.
- Reference, logged interventions: 9 kill lives, 9 kill lives with the neighbours' n_view held fixed (killNV), 6 lives with arrivals into K blocked, 6 lives with K's lateral weights zeroed, and 4 growing lives.
- Reference lesions by process fork, 64-129 lives per arm. One reference life runs to its first send at or after t_f, then os.fork() makes one child per lesion arm. Checks: every intact parent equalled the kernel twin bitwise (193 of 193), and every all-lateral child equalled the kernel lateral_off bitwise (5 of 5).

What survives:
- **Retina.** s2 is a column reflex with a passive 1-bit retina. Sense-plane lateral messages are idle, causally: blocking only sense→sense messages gives +0.04 ± 0.26 at 47 cells and −0.23 ± 0.45 at 91 cells.
- **Gain switch.** Act-cell gain is set by the GRN from its contact count (n_view):
  - w0 0.375 relays 99% of its sensor's spikes; w0 0.25 relays 59%.
  - This is now causal. Killing an enclosed act cell raises its neighbours' high-gain time share by +0.29 ± 0.05. Holding the neighbours' n_view input at its pre-kill value removes the effect (+0.03 to +0.04).
  - But the switch is slow (median 86 units) and partial. Prediction 2 (at least 5 of 6 neighbours within 15 units) is refuted: no life had more than 2.
- **Act-plane relay.** An outward-biased act-plane lateral relay (0.33 outward, 0.26 sideways, 0.15 inward) pays only in large bodies, and its sign follows size, not age (prediction 1 supported):
  - With size held at 47 cells, lateral_off gives +0.47, +0.39 and +0.47 at forks 256, 512 and 768.
  - At 72 cells it gives −0.29 (fork 512) and −0.02 ± 0.19 (fork 768; misses −26%).
  - At 91 cells it gives −1.28 ± 0.20.
  - At 91 cells the loss sits in the act-plane relay to non-K cells: −1.50 ± 0.54, captures −20%, time in the capture zone −24%. Only-K and only-sense lesions are about 0.
  - At 47 cells the decomposition does not support "the relay itself costs captures". The non-K relay gives +0.27 ± 0.21 (not significant). K's lateral input helps captures there (−0.52 ± 0.18 when removed). The parts are not additive.
- **Misses and cost.** Misses are background leaks (prediction 3 mostly supported). With size capped, doubling lam_bg gives misses ×1.98 but captures −14.6%; halving it gives misses ×0.60 and captures −1%. Lateral-lesion dF comes from reward, not cost: the non-miss cost change is at most 0.004.
- **Hotspot K.** K needs C plus neighbour input (C→K is 0.75). Prediction 4 is refuted:
  - Blocking K's lateral arrivals moves its tau-4 share only from 0.22 to 0.41, not above 0.7.
  - b = 0.25 is essentially absent with growth frozen.
  - Misses fall rather than rise.
- **Hole.** "Every life has an enclosed ring-2 act hole" is refuted: 36 of 64 lives have one at the end, at rings 1-4.

On the user's question: s2 is not a router, and it does not pool evidence in the sense plane. Its interesting message-passing features are:
1. a contact-count-driven switch that turns crowded act cells into coincidence detectors;
2. a weak, act-plane, outward relay that recruits rim motors once the body passes about 70-75 cells;
3. a hotspot that clicks on C plus neighbour coincidence.

verify.corrected_algorithm:
1. **Sensing.** A sense cell fires on essentially every receptor event (gain 2 against threshold 1), so the sense plane is a 1-bit retina. Its lateral messages carry no information that matters (a causal null at 47 and 91 cells).

2. **Relay up.** Each sense spike goes to the act cell directly above with a weight of 3·w0. The size comes from the receiver's a0 = −2 polarity read from a morphogen gradient; the same mechanism makes downward act→sense messages weakly inhibitory, and act→act lateral messages excitatory and biased outward (0.33 outward, 0.26 sideways, 0.15 inward).

3. **Gain switch.** Each act cell's GRN reads its contact count n_view (in-plane neighbours plus the cells below and above) and sets its gain:
   - few contacts: w0 0.375, a one-to-one relay;
   - crowded: w0 0.25, which needs a second input within about 2 units.
   This is causal: when a neighbour dies, the surrounding cells drift to high gain over tens to about 100 units, and not if their n_view input is held fixed. Because it reads n_view and not the face, a hidden cell above also lowers the gain.

4. **Pulling.** Rim (exposed) act cells pull the dot outward along their open face. In bodies above about 70-75 cells, act-plane lateral relays from the crowded interior to the rim add pulls toward a target over the interior. Removing them at 91 cells costs about 20% of captures and time near the target. Below about 60 cells this relay brings no detectable benefit, and lateral messages cost F overall. The sign is set by size, not age.

5. **Clicking.** The hotspot K is a crowded act cell (C→K 0.75, b 0.125). It clicks when a centre-sensor spike coincides with a second C spike or with lateral input from its act neighbours. That input supplies about half of K's spikes and half its misses, and in small bodies it also helps captures. K's tau_m drifts somewhat toward 2 when neighbours are active.

6. **Misses.** Misses are mostly background-event leaks through C and K: they scale with the background rate (×2.0 or ×0.6 when lam_bg is doubled or halved), while captures change by only −15% or −1%.

7. **Re-arming** is the world's key rule, not something evolved. Hidden cells are vestigial.
verify.simplest_alternative:
A plain column reflex: each sense cell drives the act cell above it, and lateral excitation is incidental. Its only effects would be extra twitches and clicks (cost or misses) or changes in development timing.

**Ruled out for large bodies.**
- In growth-frozen forks the non-miss cost change is at most 0.004 and the miss-cost change at most 0.07, while reward carries dF. So cost and development are excluded.
- At 91 cells, removing only the act-plane lateral input to non-K act cells costs −1.50 ± 0.54 F. Captures fall by 20% and time in the capture zone by 24%.
- The effect follows body size: about 0 to −0.3 at 72 cells and +0.4 to +0.5 at 47 cells at any age (cap experiments).
- The gain switch is a non-trivial addition with a causal n_view mechanism.

**Not ruled out for small bodies (up to about 60 cells).** There, lateral messages cost F overall (+0.47 ± 0.10 when removed) and the non-K relay shows no capture benefit (+0.27 ± 0.21). In that regime s2 behaves like the simple reflex, plus a hotspot that uses neighbour input as a coincidence partner.

interp.channels:
At the end of life every cell, of every type, emits on both channels (mask 3). Sense cells are born emitting ch1 only (emit0 is on in 15% at birth) and switch ch0 on as they mature.

Every cell listens with w0 > 0 (+1.1 sense, +1.45 to +1.6 act) and w1 < 0 (−1.0 sense, −1.375 act). The delivered weight depends on direction: w_eff[d][c] = w_c(1 + a_c·ŝ_d), where ŝ_d is the normalised (neighbour − self) morphogen difference, with a0 < 0 and a1 > 0. Act cells secrete about 4 times more morphogen (m1 0.84 in the act plane, 0.27 in the sense plane), so the same two-channel spike lands as:
- **From below (sense → act above):** ch0 +2.0 and ch1 +1.375 (the a1 = 2 anisotropy flips ch1's sign), net +3.4. Strong excitation: one arrival fires the act cell.
- **From above (act → sense below):** ch0 about 0, ch1 −1.93, net −1.9. Inhibition.
- **Same plane:** ch0 +0.9 to +1.6 against ch1 −0.85 to −1.8, so they nearly cancel.
  - Sense plane: S→J +0.37, J→J +0.14, J→C +0.18, C→J +0.10, J→S −0.36.
  - Act plane: M→M −0.11, I→M −0.29, I→K −0.51.

So ch0 and ch1 are not two messages; they are two halves of one broadcast whose net sign is set by direction. Both halves are causally required (reference lesions after t = 256, 16 lives each):
- Blocking ch1 everywhere makes lateral coupling excitatory: +17,600 spikes per life, dF −5.61 ± 0.12.
- Blocking ch0 everywhere makes lateral coupling inhibitory and cuts the upward weight to +1.4: dF −3.33 ± 0.09.

Senders and listeners: sense cells send up (excite their own motor) and sideways (weak pooling). Act cells send down (inhibit their own sensor) and sideways (weak inhibition). Hidden cells are silent.
interp.algorithm_plain:
A two-layer column reflex with a centre coincidence clicker. Its wiring signs come from a morphogen gradient.

1. A target is placed 2-6 units from the dot. Its wide halo (sigma 1.5) raises the receptor-event rate under it from 0.05 to up to 2 per unit.
2. Sense cells integrate receptor events. Outer-rim sensors fire on a single event. Interior sensors and the centre sensor need about 2 events within ~1.1 units. Their excitability is set by how many in-plane neighbours they have, so 81-85% of chain origins are true target events.
3. Each sense spike is broadcast. Because of the morphogen anisotropy it is a +3.4 kick only to the act cell directly above. Same-plane neighbours get about +0.1 to +0.37, and the act cell later answers with −1.9 to its sensor.
4. The act cell fires about 1.0 unit later (refractory 3). If it sits on the act rim, the twitch pulls the dot about 0.38 units outward on its own side, the side where the target's halo is. Pullers within 2 units of the target pull toward it (mean cos +0.65 to +0.8); pullers more than 4 units away pull away (background events).
5. The net effect is that whichever side of the disk lies under the halo drags the dot toward the target. The dot approaches at 0.3-0.4 units per unit from distances of 1.5-4, slower when the target is under the body, where pulls from all sides partly cancel (0.14-0.25).
6. Interior act cells also twitch but cannot pull (pure waste; removing them is neutral).
7. When the target comes within about 1-1.5 of the dot, the centre sensor C detects coincident events and fires the hotspot K above it. K's twitch presses the key.
   - Click rate is 0.43 per unit with the target within 0.5, 0.25 at 1-1.5, 0.07 at 2-2.5.
   - About half the clicks capture. Misses are near misses (median 1.5) made while the dot is still closing in, during the ~1-unit C→K relay.
8. Weak net-excitatory lateral coupling in the sense plane lets neighbours top up a sensor. 10% of motor spikes and 8% of clicks start in another column, worth about +0.2-0.25 F.
9. Steering and clicking are separable modules: with C silenced the dot still homes in and sits in the capture zone 37 percentage points more of the time, but captures fall by 36 per life.
10. Phenotypes are static after t = 256 (freeze has no effect). The morphogen flux that holds the signs must keep running: without it, act-plane lateral weights turn excitatory and steering falls apart.
interp.pseudocode:
```
# wiring, kept up continuously by morphogen flux (act cells secrete ~4x more than sense cells)
w_eff[d] = w0*(1 + a0*s_hat[d]) + w1*(1 + a1*s_hat[d])   # s_hat = normalised (m_neighbour - m_self)
#   from below = +3.4, from above = -1.9, same plane ~ +0.1..+0.4 (sense) / -0.1..-0.5 (act)

SENSE cell (z=0): leaky integrate-and-fire, tau 2, threshold 1
  rest b      = -0.38 if 6 in-plane contacts ... +0.2..+1.0 if <= 3 contacts   # GRN reads contact count
  on receptor event:        v += g_r      # 0.875 interior/centre (needs 2 events in ~1.1 u); 1.0-1.25 rim (1 event)
  on lateral sense spike:   v += ~0.1..0.37
  on spike from act above:  v -= 1.9      # feedback; no measurable effect on F
  if v >= 1: spike, broadcast on ch0+ch1 to all neighbours; refractory 1-1.5

ACT cell (z=1): tau 1, refractory 3
  on spike from sense below: v += 3.4  -> fires ~1.0 u after the sense spike
  on spike: twitch (kappa 1)
     if rim (open face):   pull dot 0.38 along the open face  # toward its own side = toward the halo
     if hotspot (0,0,1):   key press -> click; capture if target within 1.0 (key re-arms after twitch < 0.25)
     if interior:          nothing (wasted twitch)
  also sends -1.9 down to its own sensor; lateral -0.1..-0.5

# net behaviour
while target exists:
    the side of the disk under the halo pulls the dot toward the target (approach 0.3-0.4 u/u)
    when the target is within ~1-1.5 of the centre: C detects 2 events -> K twitches -> click (~50% captures)
```

interp.lateral_role:
Small and mainly excitatory, in the sense plane only.
- **Net weights:** in the sense plane ch0 (+1.1) and ch1 (−1.0) almost cancel, leaving S→J +0.37, J→J +0.14, J→C +0.18 and C→J +0.10, but J→S −0.36 (rim cells whose highest-morphogen neighbour is a lateral J). Act-plane net weights are slightly inhibitory: M→M −0.11, I→M −0.29, I→K −0.51.
- **Activity:** lateral arrivals give the last push for 25% of J and C spikes and 10% of S spikes. 10.7% of rim-motor spikes and 7.5% of clicks start in another column (mostly ring 1). Lateral CCG sharpness is only 1.4-1.8.
- **Causal effect:** kernel lateral_off after development −0.25 ± 0.05 (n 256), mostly through clicking: captures −2.4 and misses −6.3 per life, dist +0.12. Sense-plane-only block −0.22 ± 0.07 (n 64); act-plane-only block +0.02 ± 0.11 (n 32).
- **Development:** lateral messages matter far more there. Whole-life lateral_off −1.23, with 25 fewer captures and smaller bodies.
- **The near-zero act-plane lateral weights are themselves functional.** If they turn excitatory (morphogen transport off, or ch1 blocked), the body seizes: chem_off −2.7, of which an act-lateral block rescues +1.28 ± 0.18; ch1 block −5.6.
interp.hidden_role: None. Hidden cells (z = 2-3) appear in only 25% of lives (mean 3.2 per life, median 0) and fire 0.007 spikes per unit, about 20 times less than sense cells. Kernel hidden_off after development: dF +0.001 ± 0.008 (n 256), and +0.006 ± 0.008 with both arms frozen. Lives that grow hidden cells score lower (2.27 against 2.85, confounded with body size). They are vestigial: they only cost.
interp.vs_handbuilt:
**Reflex-like.** It is essentially the hand-built GB4 column reflex (rim sensor → motor above → pull outward; centre coincidence sensor → hotspot click), regrown by a GRN.

| measure | this body | reflex | router | speck s5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rec_other_col | 0.107 | 0 | 0.385 | 0.32 |
| lateral sense CCG sharpness | 1.4-1.8 | 1.5 | 9.4 | — |
| lateral_off after development | −0.25 | 0 | −9.3 | −5.5 |

Lateral routing exists but is a 10% add-on, not the mechanism. It does not meet the router signature.

Four differences from the hand design:
1. Interior sensors are coincidence detectors while rim sensors are single-event detectors (the hand reflex makes every steering sensor single-event).
2. The connection signs are not fixed per row. They come from a morphogen-gradient anisotropy acting on a two-channel broadcast.
3. The act cell inhibits its own sensor (−1.9), with no measurable effect.
4. Interior act cells fire uselessly.

On the same lives it is 1.04 F worse than the hand ring-3 reflex, equal to ring 2, and more robust to receptor noise. It is not inhibition-based contrast, an oscillator, a wave, winner-take-all or hotspot gating: every such candidate I could test (act-lateral inhibition, act→sense feedback, K→C) has no measurable causal effect.
interp.interesting:
1. **Signs from chemistry.** Every cell broadcasts the same two-channel spike in all directions. The receiver weights it by w_c(1 + a_c·ŝ), where ŝ is the neighbour-minus-self morphogen difference. Act cells secrete about 4 times more morphogen, so the same spike is +3.4 going up, −1.9 going down and about 0 sideways. This is directional synaptic polarity built from a chemical gradient plus a channel pair whose halves cancel laterally. It is live: stopping morphogen transport after development drifts the act-plane lateral weights to excitatory (+0.56) and costs 2.3-2.7 F, and blocking act-lateral messages rescues about 56% of that loss.
2. **Contact-count-dependent sensor tuning.** The GRN reads its contact count, so rim cells (3 or fewer neighbours) become single-event detectors (rest up to +1.0) and interior cells become 2-event coincidence detectors (rest −0.39, g_r 0.875). This filters background events (81% of motor chains start from target events, against 29% in the hand reflex). It goes with a large robustness gain: at 4 times the background noise the body loses 1.1 F less than the hand reflex and overtakes it.
3. **Steering and clicking are separate modules.** Silencing the centre sensor leaves the dot parked on the target (time in the zone +37 percentage points) while captures collapse.
4. **Negative results worth knowing:**
   - The act→sense inhibitory feedback, K→C inhibition, act-lateral inhibition and the interior motors all look like circuit motifs but have no measurable causal role.
   - An interim K→C effect (−0.29 at n 11) regressed to −0.10 ± 0.07 at n 64. A mechanism I proposed for it (protecting the key's re-arm) was refuted directly from logged lesioned lives.
5. **Performance:** this genome is a worse reflex than the hand-built one (88 cells for ring-2 performance). It wastes about 1/3 of its twitches on interior cells and clicks a little too early (about 50% precision, near misses at 1-1.5 while still approaching).
6. **Why no routing evolved here, unlike the SPECK s5 body:** with sigma 1.5 the halo reaches rim columns 2 or more units away, so a pure rim reflex already sees most targets. This is an inference, not tested.

predictions.prediction: The vertical signs are set by the act plane being the morphogen source. If act cells' secretion (sec0/sec1 of z = 1 cells) is forced down to sense-cell levels after t = 256, with phenotypes otherwise fixed, the sense→act weight falls from +3.4 toward the isotropic w0 + w1 (about +0.1 to +0.4). Act cells then almost stop firing, and F over [256, 1024] falls by at least 4, close to the motor_off level (−5.2). Conversely, making sense cells out-secrete act cells flips the up and down signs.

verify.body:
Verdict: partly confirmed. I tested 512 kernel lives and 6 to 32 reference lives per test, all new, from seeds fresh_seeds(n, seed0=31_350_000). The core of the claim holds:
- The body is a stack of sense-over-act column reflexes.
- A centre sensor that needs about two receptor events (a coincidence detector) drives the hotspot, which clicks.
- The direction-dependent synapse signs come from a morphogen difference between the two planes.
- Sideways (lateral) messages add only a little after development, and they act through reward, not cost.

Several of the specific functional claims, and three of the four predictions, fail.

Holds up (my own code):
- **Performance.** Whole-life F is +2.775 ± 0.030 (n 512). Evolved minus the ring-3 hand reflex is −1.08 ± 0.035. Evolved minus ring-2 is −0.10 ± 0.035 (z −3): slightly worse than ring-2, not "equal".
- **Column structure.** I split each cell's membrane potential at firing into its sources (6 traces). 99.0% of 12,120 rim-motor spikes would not have fired without the arrival from the sense cell below. Those senders are rim sensors (S) 72.5% of the time and interior sensors (J) 26.5%. 97.4% of hotspot spikes need the centre sensor below. Every act cell is the daughter of the sense cell under it.
- **Delivered weights** (snapshots at t 300/600/900):
  - sense → act above: +3.1 to +3.4;
  - act → sense below: −1.8 to −2.0 (ch0 about 0, ch1 −1.96);
  - lateral: −0.38 to +0.34.
  - Act cells hold morphogen m1 of 0.79-0.83 against 0.25 in the sense plane; they secrete sec1 0.233 against 0.059.
- **Secretion swap** (sense cells given act-cell secretion and vice versa, after 256, n 16). The vertical signs flip (up −2.45, down +1.86), the act plane goes silent, and dF is −3.76 ± 0.22.
- **Lateral lesion after development.**
  - Kernel lateral_off at 256 with both arms frozen: −0.29 ± 0.04 (n 512).
  - It is all reward (captures −2.6); total cost falls by 0.044.
  - Forked at 512 instead: −0.26 ± 0.04. So it is neither a cost effect nor a development-timing effect.
  - Whole-life lateral_off: −1.17, with bodies 54 cells smaller.
- **Centre sensor silenced** (n 32): −4.63 ± 0.16, captures −36 of about 41, time in the capture zone +0.35.
- **Hidden plane:** hidden_off +0.003 ± 0.008.
- **Phenotype changes after 256 are mostly harmless.** freeze −0.065 ± 0.035. pheno_fixed costs −0.80, but with divisions off in both arms only −0.09, so the loss comes from late-born cells keeping their juvenile phenotype, as they said. Still, gridded knobs flicker by one step thousands of times per life (b about 2,000, a1 about 2,900), so "static" is only approximately true.
- **Behaviour matches** (pull alignment +0.33, 71% of pulls toward the target, misses at a median 1.6, approach speed 0.34-0.42).
- **Noise robustness relative to ring-3 reproduces:** the evolved body's drop is 1.10 ± 0.06 smaller at lam_bg 0.2. At 0.2 the two only tie (1.41 against 1.43); the evolved body is ahead only at 0.4.

Refuted or corrected:
1. **"81% of motor chains start from target events, against 29% in the hand reflex" is a comparison across worlds.**
   - In catch_v1_l4, 83% of all receptor events delivered to sense cells already come from the target.
   - The ring-3 hand reflex in this world scores 0.75 (evolved 0.80).
   - This genome run in the speck world scores 0.28, the same as the hand reflex's 0.29 there.
   - Interior and centre sensors do reject about a third of background events (J 34%, C 32%); rim sensors reject almost none (3%).
2. **Interior coincidence detection has no measurable function.** I gave the interior sensors single-event knobs after 256 (b 0.25, g_r 1.125; n 32 per noise level).
   - dF −0.08 ± 0.14 at normal noise and −0.23 ± 0.12 at 4× noise.
   - Its extra loss under noise is −0.15 ± 0.20; the prediction was ≤ −2.0.
   - Target share of motor-chain origins: 0.788 against 0.794; the prediction was ≤ 0.6.
   - So the noise advantage over ring-3 is not explained by it.
   - Making the centre single-event as well adds 28 misses per life: the centre's coincidence threshold does matter, for click precision.
3. **"The lateral effect is mostly through clicking" is wrong.** Blocking only the lateral input to the centre sensor (n 32) gives dF +0.03 ± 0.11 and captures +0.2 ± 0.85, though misses fall by 5.3. That accounts for lateral_off's miss reduction but none of its capture loss. Where the capture loss comes from was not tested; steering through the sense plane is the likely route.
4. **Lateral involvement is larger, and less purely excitatory, than "a 10% add-on".**
   - Lateral input was needed to reach threshold for 39% of sense spikes, and lies upstream of 36% of rim-motor spikes (the claim said 10.7%).
   - Removing it cuts motor spikes by only 7-15% (two logged lesioned lives), so it mostly shifts spike timing.
   - Sign is set by direction: inward it excites (S→J +0.32, J→C +0.2); outward it inhibits (J→S −0.31). Rim-sensor spikes rise by 1-14% under the lesion.
5. **"The morphogen flux must keep running" is conditional.**
   - With both arms frozen, chem_off has exactly zero effect: weights computed at 256 are enough.
   - chem_off alone also regrows 45 extra cells, a confound the claim does not mention.
   - With both arms pheno_fixed, chem_off costs −2.15 ± 0.06.
6. **Prediction 3 is refuted.** In catch_speck_l4, lateral_off at 256 costs −1.30 ± 0.14, or −1.34 ± 0.13 with both arms frozen: 25% of F. Yet the share of motor spikes starting in another column there is only 0.11. That share is a poor proxy for how much F depends on lateral messages.
7. **Prediction 1 is only partly right.** Equalising act secretion (n 32) gives dF −3.64 ± 0.20, short of the predicted ≥4. The up weight inverts to about −0.5 rather than going isotropic, and act cells keep 56% of their spikes instead of nearly stopping.
8. **Prediction 4 is mostly supported.**
   - Approach speed inside 1 unit is 0.01 (predicted below 0.2).
   - P(capture|click) is 0.69 (predicted 0.6 or more).
   - Silencing the centre cuts captures 93% while the dot stays in the zone 71% of the time.
   - But only 67% of placements are captured within 8 units (89% eventually), against the predicted 85%.

tests.claim: Steering and click kinematics (pull alignment, miss distance, approach speed)
tests.experiment: Own analysis of 6 fresh traces (a3_behaviour.py)
tests.result: Pull cos +0.82 within 1 unit of the target, −0.47 beyond 6; overall +0.334, 71% toward. Captures only within distance 1; miss median 1.61. Approach 0.34-0.42 per unit at 1-2.5.

verify.corrected_algorithm:
1. The body grows about 40 columns. Each column is a sense cell with the act cell it divided off above it.
2. Each sense spike reaches the act cell above it at about +3.1 to +3.4, and one such spike fires that act cell about 1 unit later. The reply from the act cell back down is about −1.9.
3. Rim act cells pull the dot outward on their own side, so the side of the disk under the target's halo drags the dot toward it. Interior act cells twitch uselessly.
4. The centre sensor needs about 2 receptor events within about 1 unit. It drives the hotspot, and the hotspot's twitch clicks. This threshold keeps clicks precise: with a single-event centre there are about 28 more misses per life. Silencing the centre leaves the dot sitting on the target but removes about 90% of captures.
5. The direction-dependent signs are a readout of a standing morphogen difference between the planes: act cells secrete about 4 times more than sense cells.
   - Swapping the secretion flips the vertical signs and wrecks the score.
   - Freezing the weights at t 256 makes the chemistry afterwards irrelevant.
6. Sensor excitability is graded by contact count: rim sensors fire on one event, interior sensors need about 2. The interior grading has no measurable function. Giving interior sensors single-event knobs changes neither F (at normal or 4× background noise) nor the target share of motor-chain origins (about 0.79). That share is close to the base rate of 0.83 in this world anyway.
7. Sense-plane lateral coupling is weak and its sign depends on direction: excitatory inward (rim → interior and centre), inhibitory outward (interior → rim).
   - It shifts the timing of many sensor spikes but changes motor spike counts by only about 10%.
   - After development it is worth about 0.29 F, entirely through captures. Its route is not the centre sensor's lateral input (that input only adds about 5 misses); steering through the sense plane is the likely, untested route.
   - During development it is essential for growth: whole-life lateral_off gives bodies 54 cells smaller.
8. Hidden cells do nothing.
9. The body loses about 1.1 F less than the ring-3 hand reflex when background noise is raised 4 times, but the reason is unknown: it is not interior coincidence detection.
verify.simplest_alternative:
Simplest alternative: a plain column reflex, where every sense cell drives the act cell above it, rim pulls point outward, and the centre drives the hotspot, plus incidental lateral excitation. This was not ruled out for the steering sensors. Replacing the interior coincidence detectors with single-event sensors is indistinguishable in F, signal purity and noise robustness.

Only two features separate the evolved body from that alternative:
- the centre sensor's coincidence threshold, which buys click precision;
- a small but real post-development lateral contribution to captures (−0.29 F).

The alternative "lateral messages matter only through cost or development timing" is ruled out after development, and only after development:
- The effect is reward-driven, and total cost falls under the lesion.
- It is the same when the fork is moved from 256 to 512 with both arms frozen.
- It is not routed through the clicker's lateral input.

Over the whole life the lateral effect is mostly developmental (bodies end 54 cells smaller).
verify.notes:
Seeds and checks:
- Every life seed came from analysis.fresh_seeds(n, 31_350_000).
- All 16 reference traces I checked against the kernel (6 intact, 4 speck-world, 4 close-range, 2 no-override) matched its F bitwise.
- The lateral-lesioned traces matched the kernel's lateral_off fork.
- The no-override harness and no-lesion runner both matched the kernel bitwise.

Caveats:
- My "needed" counterfactual is instantaneous at threshold. It overstates spike-level dependence; the logged lesions bound that.
- Reference arms are small: n 16 for sec_swap and the single-event centre run, n 32 for the rest.
- I applied the overrides at each cell's ticks after 256 under pheno_fixed in both arms. pheno_fixed itself costs about 0.8 F (from late-born cells), so the base F in those arms is lower (about 1.9-2.3).
- I did not test where the lateral capture loss comes from (steering is the obvious candidate), and I did not re-test the channel-block lesions.
- No repo files were touched. The pilot was left alone; every job ran at nice 19 with at most 2 threads or workers each.
